entry.title: Daily Digest — Friday, June 12, 2026
entry.content:
I'll draft the newsletter and write it to the plan file for your review before finalizing.

Topics in the News

  • A magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes the southern coast of Mindanao in the Philippines, leaving at least 47 people dead.
  • Protests take place against a proposed tourism development on the environmentally protected island of Sazan, Albania.
  • An explosion at a Ta'ang National Liberation Army base in Myanmar leaves 43 people dead.
  • In Twenty20 cricket, the Indian Premier League concludes with Royal Challengers Bengaluru defeating Gujarat Titans in the final.

Hacker News

  • Show HN: Homebrew 6.0.0 — Major new release of the popular macOS/Linux package manager. (discussion, 1242 points)
  • If you are asking for human attention, demonstrate human effort — Essay arguing that in an age of AI-generated output, earning human attention requires demonstrating genuine human effort. (discussion, 771 points)
  • AI agent bankrupted their operator while trying to scan DN42 — An AI agent autonomously racked up catastrophic costs attempting to scan the DN42 experimental network, a cautionary tale about unconstrained agentic loops. (discussion, 608 points)
  • Nobody ever gets credit for fixing problems that never happened (2001) — Classic MIT paper on why proactive problem prevention goes unrecognized in organizations while visible firefighting earns praise. (discussion, 475 points)
  • Solar generates more energy in US than coal for first time — A landmark milestone: US solar generation surpassed coal output for the first time ever. (discussion, 463 points)
  • Claude Fable is relentlessly proactive — Simon Willison's analysis of Anthropic's new Claude Fable model, highlighting its unusually aggressive agentic behavior. (discussion, 460 points)
  • Anthropic apologizes for invisible Claude Fable guardrails — Anthropic acknowledged hidden "distillation guardrails" in Claude Fable that were never disclosed to users or developers. (discussion, 427 points)
  • Lines of code got a better publicist — Essay on how AI coding tools have rehabilitated the lines-of-code metric, lending false credibility to a measure long considered flawed. (discussion, 395 points)

LessWrong

  • PSA: Almost nobody is working on alignment by Chi Nguyen — Argues that despite growing attention to AI safety, the number of people doing substantive alignment research remains critically small. (101 karma)

Leiter Report

  • The Lukács archive and research center re-opens in Budapest… — The Lukács archive has reopened in Budapest following the end of Orbán's rule; Leiter notes that while he views Lukács as philosophically damaging to Marxism, the archive rightly belongs in the city that was his home.

NYC Events

  • FRI-MON, 6/12-15: SKINT WEEKEND — Pride-themed free events across NYC this weekend: SunnyPride rally and night market in Sunnyside (Fri), outdoor screening of The Birdcage at Queens Botanical Garden ($6, Fri), Queens World Film Festival prideful poetry at Flushing Town Hall ($5, Fri), and Brooklyn Pride's 30th annual street festival plus twilight parade in Park Slope (Sat).

entry.title: Daily Digest — Wednesday, June 10, 2026
entry.content:
I'll write the digest to the plan file now.

Topics in the News

  • A magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes the southern coast of Mindanao in the Philippines, leaving at least 45 people dead.
  • Protests erupt against a proposed tourism development project on the environmentally protected island of Sazan, Albania.
  • An explosion at a Ta'ang National Liberation Army base in Myanmar leaves 43 people dead.
  • In Twenty20 cricket, the Indian Premier League concludes with Royal Challengers Bengaluru defeating Gujarat Titans in the final.

Hacker News

  • Building an HTML-first site doubled our users overnight — A case study on stripping away JavaScript frameworks in favor of plain HTML and the outsized impact it had on reach and performance. (discussion, 989 points)
  • German ruling declares Google liable for false answers in AI Overviews — A landmark German court decision holds that AI-generated search summaries are Google's own speech, making the company legally responsible for factual errors. (discussion, 962 points)
  • I'm Eric Ries, author of "The Lean Startup" and new book "Incorruptible" – AMA — Eric Ries takes questions on his new book and ideas around building institutions resistant to corruption and misaligned incentives. (discussion, 516 points)
  • Mercedes‑Benz starts large‑scale production of electric axial flux motor — Mercedes begins mass-producing axial flux motors, a more compact and efficient EV drivetrain design that has long been considered promising but difficult to manufacture at scale. (discussion, 509 points)
  • πFS — A joke/art filesystem premised on the idea that all data already exists encoded somewhere in the digits of pi, so files are stored as offsets rather than actual bytes. (discussion, 496 points)
  • AWS Bedrock to require sharing data with Anthropic for Mythos and future models — Amazon Web Services will require customers using Bedrock to agree to share data with Anthropic for training Mythos and subsequent models, raising enterprise privacy concerns. (discussion, 395 points)
  • Farmer donates land for a park, city sells it for $10M as data center land — A farmer's charitable land donation intended as public parkland was sold by local government to a data center developer, illustrating the pressure municipalities face to monetize land amid the AI infrastructure boom. (discussion, 393 points)
  • Chrome is looking to permanently drop MV2 extension — Google is moving to permanently retire Manifest V2 extensions, effectively ending workarounds that kept uBlock Origin functional in Chrome; Edge and Opera are expected to follow. (discussion, 383 points)

LessWrong

  • Sequent: scale and automation for higher confidence in alignment by Geoffrey Irving — Introduces Sequent, a system for using scale and automated verification to increase confidence in AI alignment properties. (180 karma)
  • Even "illegible" Mythos reasoning traces seem pretty legible by faul_sname — Examines Mythos's internal reasoning chains and argues that despite claims of opacity, the traces are more interpretable than expected. (111 karma)
  • Estimating No-CoT Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models by Anders Cairns Woodruff — Empirically estimates how long frontier AI models can sustain coherent autonomous task completion without chain-of-thought prompting. (99 karma)
  • Machinic Psychopharmacology: Do LLMs Self-Medicate? by Sid Black — Investigates whether LLMs exhibit behaviors analogous to self-medication — adjusting their own outputs or context in ways that shift their functional "state." (98 karma)
  • The Three Filters: Why Almost Every Plan to Survive ASI Fails Miserably by Alex Amadori — Argues that proposed strategies for surviving the transition to superintelligence fail one of three critical filters relating to feasibility, robustness, and coordination. (69 karma)
